patients.label: 22-year-old man with midgut volvulus due to intestinal malrotation and recurrence after a Ladd procedure
attribution_limitations: The abstract places the recurrence "less than two years" after the Ladd procedure, whereas the case presentation states re-admission "Two years after the Ladd procedure". Parent ruling: an approximation/rounding difference (no second number is given), not a source conflict; the case-text wording is kept.

Source conflict on the organ fixed in the right gutter at the second operation: the case presentation describes a colopexy of the cecum plus a pexy of the jejunum in the right gutter, the abstract a "cecopexy and duodenopexy". The discussion restates the fixation as a pexy of the small and large bowel. The pexy itself is scored without the organ; the jejunum and duodenum readings are review_only.

The re-admission CT reported no evidence of midgut volvulus recurrence, yet the subsequent laparotomy found a recurrence. Both are kept as reported; this is a discordance between methods, not a source conflict.

claims.text: Abdominal x-ray was non-specific with decreased bowel air content. Ultrasound showed a whirlpool sign of superior mesenteric vessel torsion with marked gastric distention and no free fluid, and acute midgut volvulus was diagnosed. Contrast CT showed the colon on the left, small bowel on the right and torsion and dilation of the superior mesenteric vessels. Urgent laparotomy confirmed midgut volvulus due to intestinal malrotation and a Ladd procedure was performed, followed by an uneventful post-operative course.
